_note: Illustrative retest fixture (W5). Served when a single-screen request is a retest (links.retest_of set): it pretends the user fixed the contrast VIOLATION and added crowding, so a comparison against quick-review shows fixed/unresolved/new. Fingerprints match quick-review so the same issue lines up across runs. Not real audit output.

summary.perceived_purpose: Sign-up screen for a personal budgeting app with a plan choice.
summary.first_impression: Price contrast is fixed, but the plan cards still read as decoration and the header is now crowded.
summary.headline: Contrast resolved; plan selection is still easy to miss and the header is crowded.

findings.title: Primary action competes with the plan cards for attention
findings.location: scr_1 (uploaded screenshot), hero and plan cards
findings.observed: The 'Get started' button and three equally saturated plan cards still carry similar visual weight.
findings.expected: One dominant primary action, with the plan choice clearly subordinate or a required step.
findings.impact: First-time users hesitate between the cards and the button.

evidence.note: Salience estimate over the captured viewport

findings.recommendation: Lower the plan cards' saturation and add the caption 'Choose a plan'.

steps: Re-run the primary_action test on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: Personas name 'Get started' as the first element they would tap.

findings.limitations: Salience inferred from a static screenshot.

findings.title: Simulated personas did not recognize the plan selector as a choice
findings.observed: 2 of 3 simulated personas still described the plan cards as informational.
findings.expected: Personas identify the plan cards as a required choice before continuing.
findings.impact: Users may proceed without choosing a plan.

persona_signals.observation: The plan cards look like feature highlights.
Unsure whether tapping a card does anything.

findings.recommendation: Make the plan cards read as a selectable group with a visible selected state.

steps: Re-run the comprehension test on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: At least 2 of 3 simulated personas identify the plan cards as a choice.

findings.limitations: Simulated persona behavior from a static screenshot; not human participant research.

findings.title: Terms text under the button is unlikely to be read
findings.location: scr_1 (uploaded screenshot), below the primary button
findings.observed: A two-line legal notice in small light text still sits directly under 'Get started'.
findings.expected: Legal consequences are visible before the action, or the notice is short and legible.
findings.impact: Users may accept terms without noticing; low user impact.
findings.recommendation: Shorten the notice to one line at body size and link to the full terms.

steps: Check the notice text size and position on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: Notice is one line at body text size.

findings.limitations: Text size estimated from a static screenshot.

findings.title: Header logo and title are crowded after the layout change
findings.observed: The logo and the title now sit with little spacing between them at the top of the screen.
findings.expected: Clear separation between the logo and the screen title.
findings.impact: The header reads as one block; the title loses prominence.
findings.recommendation: Restore vertical spacing between the logo and the title.

steps: Check the spacing between the logo and title on the revised screen.
retest.expected_result: There is clear separation between the logo and the title.

findings.limitations: Spacing estimated from a static screenshot.

An app that wants me to sign up; I can read the price now.

tests.majority_answer: Unsure whether the plan cards do anything

persona_summary.disclaimer: Results are simulated persona behavior, not human participant research.

rule_results.note: Price text contrast now meets the minimum in the captured state

limitations.text: Static screenshot: semantics, keyboard operability, focus order, dynamic states, and performance were not tested.
Simulated personas reason over a salience-weighted snapshot and may skip secondary text by design. Results are simulated persona behavior, not human participant research.
